Turo (RICARDO FIGUEIREDO) BEWARE

At 5:22pm TODAY I gained access to this model 3 via the app. Screenshots for proof. I had a Uber drop me and my kids off. I installed my kid’s car seats, got them in the car and the issues began.

Host is dishonest.

As soon as I turned the car on, I get an alert “Rear tire tread depth low - Schedule service  
Inspect tires for rotation/replacement.”   
The car was within 2 miles from my apartment. As I’m driving back at 20mph, the car starts shaking. 

Once I parked I sent the host the alerts and told him what’s going on. His response was  
 “Please return the car immediately if you are not happy.  
The message is juts a reset.  
The car not was shaking  
I can't have a bad review  
I prefere you return the car and I'II refund you 100%.” 

I think that response alone rests my case. 

Be careful renting from Turo. This is my first time ever having a host like this and a bad car. This car has 140K+ miles. I look up cars on Carvana often. A lot of these hosts are buying high mileage cars online and then renting them out on Turo. 

The host picked up his vehicle, never told me had got it and did not end my trip. The original message after informing the host made me immediately call support. They offered to get me another vehicle and cover the difference. I declined.

In the past, I drove a Tesla model 3 from eastern NC to a city near Detroit (Turo rental). Didn’t have any issues with how the car drove.

I genuinely needed the car. I knew I should’ve got a rental from the airport, but I didn’t want to spend too much. I thought that’s what Turo was for. A cheaper alternative. Turo itself isn’t bad but hosts… you never know.

Has anyone else noticed the boat rentals taking over Lake Ivanhoe?

Has anyone else noticed the boat rentals at Lake Ivanhoe in downtown Orlando getting a little out of control?

There’s a newer company that started operating around July, and they’ve been taking up **2 of the 3 trailer parking spots**at the public boat ramp with their trucks and trailers. From what I’ve seen, they’ll leave them there **from sunup to sundown**, essentially using the public trailer spaces as their staging area for the entire day.

On top of that, their rental “car boats” and jet skis are being left **tied up along the small public dock for hours at a time while they wait for customers**. The dock is already tiny, so when most of it is occupied by rental boats, it leaves very little room for everyone else to load, unload, launch, or even fish.

I’m not against people running legitimate businesses or renting boats. If they have the proper permits, fine. But I’m having a hard time understanding how a public boat ramp with only **three trailer spaces** can effectively have two of those spaces occupied all day by one commercial operation, while their rental boats also sit at the public dock for hours.

Most small public boat ramps I’ve used have some kind of short-term loading/unloading restriction, often around 10 minutes, specifically so one person or business can't tie up the dock all day.

Am I the only one who has noticed this, or has anyone else had trouble getting a parking spot or access to the dock because of the rental companies?

And if anyone actually knows what the rules are for commercial boat rentals using the Lake Ivanhoe public ramp, I’d genuinely like to know. I’m not looking to start some anti-business crusade. I just don't think a public boat ramp should effectively become a private staging area when there are only three trailer spaces to begin with.

Hot take: Orlando needs more boring, comfortable third spaces open past 7

Maybe I'm just getting older, but Orlando feels weirdly split between places you buy a ticket for and loud, spendy spots. I live on the east side and after work I'm usually hunting for something very unglamorous: a safe, calm place to sit for an hour with a puzzle book or my headphones. I don't want to drink, network, or fight for a table.

  
Whenever someone asks about third spaces the answers are basically the same: coffee shops, breweries, or parks. Coffee shops are great, but most close early and you don't want to be 'camping' if there's a line. Breweries aren't a third space if you don't drink or just want quiet. Parks are awesome in daylight, but after dark they can feel iffy.

  
This feels less like a personal taste issue and more like a city design problem. We build tons of places for tourists, commuters, and events, but not many spots for residents to just exist indoors in the evening.

  
I'm not asking for freebies or to loiter. I would happily pay a small cover or membership for a clean, well-lit, staffed spot with comfortable seating, decent hours, and basic rules. Libraries exist, but they close too early if you work a normal day.

  
Anyone else feel this, or am I missing obvious options that aren't cafes or bars?

If you’ve ever tried finding happy hours around Orlando, you’ve probably come across GoldenBuzz. It’s useful, but I always felt like there was a lot of room to make the experience better.

So I built **Pour Happy**: [**pourh.com**](http://pourh.com/)

The goal is to make finding a happy hour around Orlando ridiculously easy.

You can:  
Browse happy hours by area  
See the actual days, times, drinks, and food specials  
Sort by top voted, A–Z, starting soon, or happening right now  
Upvote/downvote spots  
Save favorites  
Submit happy hours that are missing

Check em out, thank me later 🤜🤛

Winter Park's new "Dog Park Tax": $2-$3/hr for Orlando residents

Hey r/Orlando,

If you use Lake Baldwin Park for anything, you need to know about this.

On September 9, the Winter Park City Commission voted 5-0 to move forward with a paid parking pilot at Lake Baldwin Park and Dinky Dock, targeting Spring 2027. ([Orlando Weekly coverage here](https://www.orlandoweekly.com/news/orlando-area-news/winter-park-advances-plan-for-paid-parking-at-lake-baldwin-park-dinky-dock/)) ([Bungalower coverage here](https://bungalower.com/2026/09/14/not-from-winter-park-parking-at-lake-baldwin-and-dinky-dock-could-cost-2-3-an-hour/))

Here's how it works:

* If you don't live in Winter Park: $2 to $3 per hour, or $20/day, paid through an app
* If you do live in Winter Park: free, but you have to register your car and prove residency every year (capped at 2 vehicles per household)

I visit this park twice a day with my two Labs. I live in Orlando, two blocks from the Winter Park line. This park is the highlight of my day.

**Here's what actually happens at this park every morning.** The regulars are almost all retirees. Fixed incomes. Same people, same dogs, same benches. For a lot of them this is their only daily social interaction. Most of them don't live in Winter Park. At $2 to $3 an hour, twice a day, that's $120 to $180 a month. They can't afford that. They'll stop coming.

**The city says Winter Park taxpayers are subsidizing Orlando visitors.** Except Winter Park didn't buy this land. The 23 acres were given to the city in 1972 through a federal program and a donation from the Catholic Diocese. Development was funded by a state grant. The trail was built with FDOT money. The playground was built by a private corporate grant. All of us paid for this park, not just Winter Park property owners.

**I'm not a lawyer, but there's a state rule that seems to directly address this.** Florida Administrative Code Rule 62D-5.059(6) says that parks built with state recreation grants can't charge non-residents more just because they don't pay local taxes. The city has to prove that out-of-town visitors cause a specific additional cost burden that residents don't. They haven't done that. Their entire argument on the record is "they don't pay our property taxes," which is exactly the reasoning this rule restricts.

**The revenue math is a joke.** The city projects $100,000 in gross revenue. Their budget is $247 million. That's less than 0.05%. And that's before the app vendors, payment processors, enforcement staff, and admin costs take their cut. The net might be $40k to $60k. That's not a revenue strategy. That's a rounding error.

**The spillover into neighborhoods is guaranteed.** Due to the geography around the lake, there are only a handful of residential streets nearby. Those streets are going to feel this immediately. Nobody is paying $3 to walk their dog for 30 minutes when free parking is a few blocks away. **The Saturday morning run club will just park somewhere else** because they're going out for a run anyway. What's an extra two or three blocks when you're already running? Winter Park's own staff admitted during the meeting that spillover is a real possibility.

**The volunteer group that actually helps maintain this park wasn't even consulted.** The Friends of Winter Park Dog Park is a nonprofit that organizes cleanups, fills holes, picks up trash, and maintains grounds. They take real burden off the city's parks staff. A lot of those volunteers are the same non-residents this proposal would charge.

**And Winter Park already tried this.** In 2010 they approved a $75 per dog fee at Lake Baldwin. Five months later they voted 5-0 to repeal it after community backlash. Same park, same idea.

**If you care about this, here's what you can do right now (60 seconds):**

Send a short, respectful email to the full Commission telling them you oppose paid parking at Lake Baldwin. They still have to draft and vote on the formal ordinance before this becomes law.

* **Email the Commission:** [MayorandCommissioners@cityofwinterpark.org](mailto:MayorandCommissioners@cityofwinterpark.org)
* **CC the City Clerk (gets it on public record):** [cityclerk@cityofwinterpark.org](mailto:cityclerk@cityofwinterpark.org)

You don't have to write a novel. Just tell them who you are, that you use the park, and that you oppose paid parking. Every email counts.
